headline: Biman forms probe body over technical glitch on PM's flight
summary: A four-member committee has been tasked to investigate a spoiler glitch that delayed Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's flight from Japan by over four hours.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has formed a four-member investigation committee to probe a technical glitch that occurred on the aircraft carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman from Japan.
The committee has been ordered to submit its findings within seven working days.
The probe will focus on the actual cause and nature of the technical fault, reviewing the steps taken to ensure flight safety and airworthiness.
The investigation will also assess the impact of the flight delay and passenger inconvenience, as well as the effect on the national carrier's institutional image.
The incident occurred on Thursday, October 29, when the flight was scheduled to depart from Japan at 6:18 PM local time.
After boarding and pushback, a spoiler-related glitch signal appeared in the cockpit as the plane moved toward the runway.
The takeoff was canceled, and the aircraft departed for Dhaka after more than four hours of technical inspections and repairs.
The Prime Minister's flight landed safely at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 2:48 AM on Friday, October 30.
caption:
A spoiler glitch delayed the Prime Minister's flight from Japan by over 4 hours. Now, Biman is launching a full investigation.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has formed a four-member investigation committee to probe a technical glitch that occurred on the aircraft carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman from Japan.

The committee has been ordered to submit its findings within seven working days.

The probe will focus on the actual cause and nature of the technical fault, reviewing the steps taken to ensure flight safety and airworthiness.

The investigation will also assess the impact of the flight delay and passenger inconvenience, as well as the effect on the national carrier's institutional image.

The incident occurred on Thursday, October 29, when the flight was scheduled to depart from Japan at 6:18 PM local time.

After boarding and pushback, a spoiler-related glitch signal appeared in the cockpit as the plane moved toward the runway.

The takeoff was canceled, and the aircraft departed for Dhaka after more than four hours of technical inspections and repairs.

The Prime Minister's flight landed safely at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 2:48 AM on Friday, October 30.

headline_marked: PBI [[takes friend into custody]] over death of former Air Force officer
headline: PBI takes friend into custody over death of former Air Force officer
summary: Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip was detained for questioning after CCTV footage showed him with KM Tahsif Souri shortly before the officer went missing.
details: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has detained Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip for questioning in connection with the death of former Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri.
Dip was taken into custody from a house on Babar Road in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, after CCTV footage showed him with Tahsif shortly before the officer disappeared.
During interrogation, Dip claimed that while they were at Mazar Basti, they were chased by some people, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dip managed to escape.
PBI officials stated they are not fully convinced by Dip's statement and are continuing their investigation into other possibilities, including the possibility of strangulation.
Tahsif's body was recovered from the Turag river near the Rajabari ferry terminal on Monday. A plateless motorcycle, believed to be Tahsif's, was also recovered nearby.
KM Tahsif Souri gained public attention for reportedly recording a video showing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country on August 5, 2024.
caption:
A friend is in custody as PBI probes the death of the man who recorded Sheikh Hasina's departure.

The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has detained Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip for questioning in connection with the death of former Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri.

Dip was taken into custody from a house on Babar Road in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, after CCTV footage showed him with Tahsif shortly before the officer disappeared.

During interrogation, Dip claimed that while they were at Mazar Basti, they were chased by some people, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dip managed to escape.

PBI officials stated they are not fully convinced by Dip's statement and are continuing their investigation into other possibilities, including the possibility of strangulation.

Tahsif's body was recovered from the Turag river near the Rajabari ferry terminal on Monday. A plateless motorcycle, believed to be Tahsif's, was also recovered nearby.

KM Tahsif Souri gained public attention for reportedly recording a video showing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country on August 5, 2024.
